text.p: - The proposed new tax to be levied on those buying foreign currencies in cash contradicts both Russia's internal legislation and IMF regulations.
- The Moscow government has apparently decided to bail out the troubled car-maker Moskvich.
- Ulyanovsky Avtozavod, one of Russia's biggest off-road vehicle producers, launches a new model next year.
- The rejection by the Federation Council of a draft law on courts puts the already shaky judicial mechanism in an even more precarious position.
- The government has had the upper hand in a bitter dispute with the troubled car-maker AvtoVAZ over the future of the debt-laiden company.
- Russia's law and order authorities seem to have lost control over the criminal world, something which could prompt an open war between society and gangland lords.
- The communists stand to lose the last round of regional elections this weekend and with it their last chance of scooping a majority in the upper house of parliament.
- Exhibits in all Russian museums will soon get special forgeproof electronic identity marks supposed to help protect them from theft inside as well as outside the country.
